content.text: On the Work In Progress report, the

filter does not offer every asset that is on the report. Where two different vehicles happen to share the same unit number, the filter lists only one of them — and it shows that one's vehicle identification number against the shared unit number. The other vehicle is simply not in the list, so typing its vehicle identification number brings up nothing at all.

The filter is meant to let you type either the unit number or the vehicle identification number. For these vehicles the second half of that promise does not work, and a service manager searching for a truck by the number on its windscreen concludes the truck has no open work, when in fact it has.
On today's test data six vehicles are affected across five shared unit numbers. The clearest one belongs to customer
, which has two different trucks both numbered

Why it matters quietly rather than loudly: the filter looks like it is working. You type a unit number, you get a result, and nothing tells you that a second vehicle with that same number exists and has been left out.

The two other filters on the same toolbar are complete, so this is specific to the Asset filter and not a general scope problem:
Distinct values actually on the report

So the filter is not limited to the rows currently loaded — that part works correctly, and it works across all four tabs and both locations. The problem is only that the list is built one entry per unit number. Also ruled out: it is not the date range (the same six are missing on a narrower range), and it is not the
case alone — that one has the additional oddity that its option carries no vehicle identification number even though the work order does.
Every asset that appears on the report should be offered in the Asset filter, and typing either identifier should find it. The Work In Progress specification, version 9, requires (S7-R4):

The toolbar has an Asset filter, a searchable type-ahead multi-select listing the assets present across all open jobs in the current scope. Each option shows the unit number and the vehicle identification number, and the user's typed text matches against EITHER the unit number OR the vehicle identification number.
Two vehicles that share a unit number are still two assets present on the report, so both should be listed and both identification numbers should match.
For non-vehicle assets, note that this field holds the unit's serial number rather than a true vehicle identification number — that is expected and is not what this ticket is about.

The Asset filter offers one entry per unit number. Where two vehicles share a unit number only one is listed, the listed entry shows only that one's identification number, and the other vehicle's identification number matches nothing typed into the filter. Six vehicles are affected on the current test data.

No screenshot is attached, and the reason is stated rather than implied: this session could not open the application's screens at all. The application front end would not accept the browser session available to this run, and the one route that produces a signed-in browser could not be used because it would have reset a sign-in shared with two other testers working on other branches at the same time. What is written above was read directly from the data the Asset filter is built from, and the full response is saved with our evidence so the six missing vehicles can be confirmed without repeating the work.

Specification: Work In Progress, Confluence page 703660034, version 9, Story 7 (S7-R4) — the "across all open jobs in the current scope" wording was added in version 9 on 2026-08-05.

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Work In Progress report specification, version 9, requirement S7-R4, which says: "The toolbar has an Asset filter, a searchable type-ahead multi-select listing the assets present across all open jobs in the current scope. Each option shows the unit number and the vehicle identification number, and the user's typed text matches against EITHER the unit number OR the vehicle identification number." Two different vehicles that share a unit number are two assets present in scope, so both belong in the list.
